description:
We are a group of friends who are passionate about Data Analysis and user experiences and interested in Space physiology and human performance. 

We want to develop a robust and comprehensive application for long-term health monitoring.
summary:
We developed an app that addresses two main issues with Deep-space exploration:
1. Missions lacking a flight surgeon or a medical specialist, that can help during emergency situations.
2. Lacking knowledge regarding the extent of the human physical response during prolonged deep space missions resulting in the need of long term monitoring usually done by wearable instruments that might cause irritation
details:
The project is a fullstack web app that runs a server on the cloud, with multiple services provided to each astronaut on the flight. The goal: constant vital monitoring to assess astronaut health without any wearables or skin contact.

Astronauts are not fully monitored in real time, and when venturing into deep space, communication with a medical officer is not assured. The project attempts to solve this by providing solutions based on innovative telemedicine algorithms and agentic workflows that can be ran locally such that the spaceship can treat emergency situations when a medical officer is unavailable.

This kind of integration of telemedicine methods was never done before on a singular deployed system and does not exist in the space industry.

The project is mostly written in Python, while also deploying an HTML, Javascript and CSS based frontend. It also uses docker to deploy the web server on Google Cloud based on Firebase.

It uses local algorithms and ML models for inference, and relies on a local, customer-grade webcam and microphone.

The project implements the following services:

1. A video analysis algorithm that estimates heart rate and breathing rate, synchronized on the same timestamps to accurately calculate Cardio-Respiratory Coupling.

2. A speech analysis algorithm that computes a statistical score, indicating on risks of developing lung or neck area edemas.

3. Analysis of health measurements, to present specific vital trends (e.g immune response indicators, sleep quality, calcium levels in serum and urine, etc.).

4. An agentic model and harness (RAG based context), capable of guiding the responding astronaut in real time on how to treat another crew member in emergency situations.

To create this app, we considered the journey to deep space, and that not all missions have a medical officer onboard. We thought about the limitations of deployed hardware - since we did not have more than what the project requires at the moment, we limited monitoring to what was available at hand for evaluation.
